CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, OCTOBER 28, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:44 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Manuel Arana, Chief of Police
ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria
  del Pilar Avalos, Council Member Gil Hurtado and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas
1
PROPERTY USE ADMIN/
PERMITS  Following the conclusion of the Public Hearing, the City Council
  unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2025-35-CC entitled Resolution of
  the City Council of the City of South Gate, approving the live
  entertainment permit for “The Place @ Tweedy” to have live
  entertainment at 3703 Tweedy Boulevard (“Project Site”), subject to the
  conditions set forth in Planning Commission Resolution No. 2025-10 and
  any limitations and/or conditions the City Council may wish to impose by
  motion of Mayor Davila and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, stated John Signal,
  Planning Manager, will be giving the presentation.

  John Signal, Planning Manager, gave the presentation.

  Mayor Davila is pleased to see a business finally coming in. That building
  has been vacant for a long time and has become an eyesore.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney asked Mayor Davila if the applicants’
  representative is present to speak first and be identified for the record.

  Silvestre Madrigal Jr., 9600 Gallatin Road, Downey, CA., grew up in
  Downey and has seen the city’s turnaround with the businesses. The City
  of Bellflower also with SteelCraft. Mr. Madrigal has a passion for business
  and business owners and making an effort to help business owners with
  their dream.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

1
PROPERTY USE ADMIN/
PERMITS CONT’D  Ms. Pereira, Mr. Madrigal’s fiancé, is in support of him helping businesses
  succeed.

  Speaker spoke in support of the proposed project.

  Genesis Clara-Martinez, applicant, is excited and honored to be able to
  enter into this community.

  Adela Herrera, South Gate resident, is in support of the proposed project.

  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

EMAILS  Eleven emails in support of the proposed project and zero in opposition.

  Council Member Hurtado is in support of the proposed project but asked
  how the business is going to control the noise from not impacting the
  residents.

  Mr. Madrigal stated a noise study report was done and it was
  recommended that a couple of sound bearing walls and limiting the
  musicians. He also stated that the business closes early, at about 9 or 10
  o’clock.

  Council Member Hurtado asked about the alcohol and if it would affect
  the business to stop serving early.

  Mr. Madrigal doesn’t believe it will affect the business.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked if there was outreach to the community in
  that area? And if so, what was the feedback from the community?

  Mr. Madrigal believes there was no outreach to the community. Letters
  were mailed to everyone to attend tonight’s City Council meeting.

  Mr. Houston asked Mr. Perez if the noticing was done through the
  surrounding community as per normal protocols?

  Mr. Perez stated that there isn’t a direct requirement for the applicant to do
  outreach around the project. The city has requirements in the code that
  public hearings need to be advertised to property owners and residents,
  within 500 ft.

  Mr. Signal stated the city mailed 900 joint notices; the radius requirement
  is 1,000 ft. to neighbors, owners, occupants, and residents.

  Page 2 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

1
PROPERTY USE ADMIN/
PERMITS CONT’D  Councilwoman Avalos asked the capacity of the facility? How many
  patriots will it hold?

  Mr. Signal stated that based on the California Building Code it was used.
  The size is about 7,750. It would be a little over 500 people.

  Councilwoman Avalos stated that the security for the is facility will be
  done through cameras. What does the Municipal Code state regarding
  large gatherings?

  Mr. Madrigal’s understanding is there will be security on site.

  Councilwoman Avalos is requesting that be included in the conditions. She
  also asked for clarification as to the hours of operation.

  Mr. Madrigal believes 9 p.m.

  Councilwoman Avalos stated Friday and Saturday until 10 p.m. is fine but
  Sunday until 9 p.m. would be reasonable.

  Councilwoman Avalos is requesting an email be sent to the police
  department if the noise level goes above.

  Council Member Hurtado mentioned a business in Hollydale was going to
  have live music and the residents were not in support to due to the noise.
  The business owner stated that there would be no speakers or amplifiers.

  Councilwoman Avalos asked who will be applying for the ABC liquor
  license and will there be a time for children to play at the playground.

  Mr. Madrigal stated there is no time set. And he will be applying for the
  ABC liquor license.

  Council Member Rios is in support of the proposed project.

  Vice Mayor Barron thanked the applicant for making this investment to
  the South Gate community.

  Mayor Davila is in support of the proposed project.

  Mr. Houston asked for specificity with regards to security for evenings on
  a Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

  Mr. Madrigal stated the security can be from 5 p.m. to close.

  Page 3 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025
1
PROPERTY USE ADMIN/
PERMITS CONT’D  Mr. Houston stated 6 p.m. on Friday and Saturday. If any issue occurs it
  can be addressed.

  Mr. Madrigal is very appreciative of everyone’s comments.

  Mr. Houston asked for clarification on the hours of operation. Sunday –
  Thursday opened from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. and then Friday and Saturday
  opened from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m.

  Mr. Madrigal stated that was correct.

  Mr. Houston asked for clarification on the schedule of entertainment and
  the alcohol sales.

  Mr. Madrigal stated the business will close at 10:00 p.m. so, until 9:30
  p.m.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE-NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Brenda Rojas, Renoa Avenue stated filing 75 odor and dust complaints
  with the city, AQMD and LA County Department of Public Health on
  Green Wise Soil Technologies.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue, stated that illegal dumping is happening on
  city-owned lots specifically between Nebraska and Tweedy. She stated
  Robert Sanchez attended the Planning Commission on the 7th of October
  wanting to thank the Planning Commission for the pickle courts at the
  parks. Ms. Ruiz believes Mr. Sanchez was probably at the wrong meeting.
  She will be forwarding an article from NPR about investigations into ICE
  raids using vehicles that have had their license plate changes.

  Alicia Flores Rivera, 10325 Garfield spoke about the odor coming from
  Green Wise Soil Technologies and what the city is planning on doing
  about it.

  Evelyn Chacon represents AYSO and asked if anything discussion was
  had regarding AYSO’s concerns at Hollydale Park.

EMAILS  Central Basin Municipal Water District Employee speaking anonymously
  out of fear of retaliation. The employee shares serious concerns about
  former Board Member Martha Camacho Rodriguez past conduct.

  Page 4 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE-NON-AGENDA
ITEMS (EMAILS) CONT’D  Asia Mason expresses appreciation for the reopening of Circle Park. She is
  also voicing serious concerns about reports of bird activity at Greenwise,
  potentially posing for a public health risk to nearby residents.

  Juan Carlos Chavez stating Greenway Soil Technologies got a violation
  for having too much product on site. The company is reporting fire hazard
  if mounds are covered.

  Anonymous email asking why the City of South Gate granted GWS a
  CEQA exemption in 2017.

  Anonymous South Gate resident voice serious concerns about the ongoing
  file odors at the Hollydale and Circle Park area which have been persistent
  and worsening over the years.

  Circle Park resident questioned why GWS composting facility on Miller
  Way has operated over a decade emitting strong odors and dust without
  being required to conduct odor studies.

  Cindy Lopez submitted a public comment expressing concern about a
  persistent odor affecting Circle Park area.

  Ella Gonzalez expressed concern about the lack of lighting at Hollydale
  Park, which forces the children to practice sports in unsafe dark
  conditions.

  Roberto Sanchez asked if the State of the City Address be on YouTube.
  Why is it held on the time when most residents are working. Will anyone
  be able to ask questions on the State of the City Address.

  Maria Chavez submitted a public comment regarding the upcoming State
  of the City Address expressing hope the presentation will reflect city’s
  future financial situation rather than the polished version.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Rob Houston, City Manager, appreciates the healthy discussion, concern
  and irritation that’s going on in the neighborhood south of GWS/UWS
  properties. The city has been aware of those and been working with
  conversations both with the operator but also trying to get an
  understanding of where LA County Public Health is at when it comes to
  the regulatory process. Gabe Perez, Director of Community Development,
  will have additional updates. Steve Costley, Director of Parks &
  Recreation, will provide an update on the park situation where AYSO
  practices.

  Mayor Davila is requesting a report on any violations UWS might have.

  Page 5 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Mr. Houston stated the city is waiting from the regulatory agencies’ report.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, cautioned City Council that this item comes
  up before the Council in the section dealing not on the agenda. The law
  allows an opportunity to briefly discuss it. He recommends this item be
  agendized for further discussion.
  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, stated no updates.

  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation, reiterated that AYSO was
  created in 1993 for region 106 in this area and with the understanding that
  the park space being used was not lit and did not have anytime soon
  possibility of being lit. AYSO does not currently have a permit that goes
  past dusk at the park.

  Mr. Costley stated as to the lighting at the facility, the city has put in grant
  applications for construction designs. As to the bathrooms, in 2017, they
  were remodeled in consultation with AYSO at the time. The city removed
  the doors and used a barrier-looking bathroom due to the homeless and
  unsavory people who decided to habitat the bathrooms.

  Mr. Costley highlighted upcoming community events.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, addressed the GWS,
  Green Wise Technologies issue. The County Public Health Department
  was invited to attend a Council Meeting for a presentation on their
  regulatory requirements.

  Vice Mayor Barron informed AYSO that the city is working on a solution.
  He received an invitation to go to the park tomorrow.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administration Services, stated that at the next
  City Council Meeting of November 11th, City Manager and himself will be
  co-presenting a finance update.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, mentioned that November
  10th is the Marine Corps’s 250th Birthday.

  Manny Arana, Chief of Police, thanked Mr. Hamilton for his service
  because he’s a Marine and once a Marine always a Marine. He is excited
  to present tonight and an honor to represent the Police Department.

  The Chief stated that illegal dumping is a serious crime and it’s a problem
  in the City of South Gate. He invited the public to attend the Trunk or
  Treat on the 30th from 5:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Seaborg Way.

  Page 6 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Rob Houston, City Manager, stated that the swearing-in of the new Chief
  of Police is tomorrow at 5:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers. He also
  mentioned there will be a second presentation at the November 25th
  Council Meeting.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, stated no updates.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, was going to request a quarterly budget
  update and is pleased to know it will be placed on the agenda for the
  Council Meeting of November 11th.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, addressed the State of the City comment.

  Council Member Avalos addressed the issues the community will face due
  to the government shutdown. She mentioned Lynwood Unified School
  District and LAUSD will be closing schools due to low enrollments.

  Council Member Hurtado stated Council Members don’t always agree
  with one another. There will be lively debates.

  Council Member Hurtado received an email from a friend whose child
  plays in AYSO asking why the city cannot have lights at Hollydale Park.
  He provided an explanation.

  Council Member Rios concurs with Council Members’ comments
  regarding AYSO. He thanked Mr. Perez for explaining the issues with
  Green Wise Technologies. He’s very pleased with the three Public Works
  employees that came up with an innovative idea to address the sidewalk
  issues. The employees deserve recognition.

  Vice Mayor Barron attended the South Gate Kiwanis Day of Service
  which is their monthly cleanup. He mentioned great people that are part of
  the organization which are doing great work. He highlighted a student
  advisor at KIPP, Denise Gomez. Ms. Gomez is a teacher. He congratulated
  Chief Arana once again.

  Vice Mayor Barron stated last Saturday, the SELA Kiwanis had their Day
  of Service and they partnered with LA Community Service and LA
  Federation of Labor at their food bank facility.

  Vice Mayor Barron thanked the police department and Sean Palos for
  organizing a neighborhood watch meeting on his block. He mentioned that
  this Saturday, the South Gate Junior Athletic Association is going to be
  hosting their fifth Annual Toy Drive. This is done every year to raise toys
  that get donated to the Santa Cop program with the South Gate Police
  Department. Paula Torres from Compatior asked him to remind the

  Page 7 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  community that they are taking registrations for Christmas with Santa
  2025. The last day to register is November 7, 2025.

  Mayor Davia congratulated Chief Arana once again.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10 were approved by motion of
  Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council Member Hurtado. Items
  7 and 9 were pulled for separate discussion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

2
STATEMENTS OF
ECONOMIC INTEREST  The City Council unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2025-36-CC
  entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California, amending the City’s Conflict of Interest Code during Consent
  Calendar.

3
CIVIL SERVICE ADMIN  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B & C during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-37-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, amending and restating Resolution
  No. 6377 (Rules and Regulations for the Administration of Civil
  Service Procedures);

  b. Personnel Management Rules; and

  c. Remove the Hiring Rules from a resolution and move them into an
  Administrative Regulation.

4
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. 2025-03-CC with T.Y. Lin
  International, to provide additional construction management and
  inspection services for the construction of for the Citywide Residential
  Resurfacing, Phase IV, City Project No. 699-ST (“the Residential
  Resurfacing Project IV”), at a cost not to exceed $112,537; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Page 8 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

5
PARKS  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B & C during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Change Order No. 4 in the amount of $80,000 to Contract No. 2023-
  58-AC with Executive Management Security Services;

  b. Authorized the Director of Administrative Services to execute Change
  Order No. 4 in a form acceptable to the City Attorney; and

  c. The reappropriation of $80,000 from Salaries (Acct No. 100-401-61-
  5101) to Professional Services (Acct No. 100-401-61-6101) to fund
  the change order.
6
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C & D during
  Consent Calendar:

  a. Maintenance Services Agreement (Contract No. 2025-71-CC) with CJ
  Concrete Construction, for sidewalk repair services, for an amount not
  to exceed $782,000;

  b. Authorized the City Manager to approve and execute amendments to
  the Professional Services Agreement up to a cumulative amount of
  $193,000;

  c. A budget amendment to add funding for part-time Engineering Aide
  assistance and transfer $125,000 in Gas Tax Funds from the Sidewalk
  Maintenance Services budget to fully fund the position which is
  needed to provide inspections services; and

  d. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.
7
LEGAL OPERATIONS  The City Council unanimously approved (as amended) items A & B
  during Consent Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-72-CC) with PermiTech to provide
  wireless consulting services; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

  AMENDMENT: Approve the contract as a one-year term, authorize City
  Manager or his designee to extend the contract for up to two years and the
  $50,000 is for three years, not one year.

  Page 9 of 11
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 28, 2025

8
DEEDS &
EASEMENTS  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Grant Deed from GVD Commercial Properties, Inc. and Monte Mac
  No. 1, LP to secure right-of-way for street purposes as a part of the
  development located at Firestone Boulevard and El Paseo Street, at no
  cost to the City; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Deed in a form acceptable to the
  City Attorney.

9
LEGAL OPERATIONS  The City Council unanimously continued items A & B to the next
  regularly scheduled City Council Meeting of November 11, 2025:

  a. Approving Attorney Retainer Agreements with the law firms of (1)
  Liebert Cassidy Whitmore; (2) Aleshire & Wynder; (3) Lewis
  Brisbois; (4) Rothans, Carpenter & Dumont; and Frost Brown Todd,
  LLP to continue to provide legal services to the City related to
  consulting, representational and legal services and

  b. Authorize the City Manager to execute such agreements in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.
10
MINUTES  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar

  a. The Special and Regular Meeting minutes of September 9, 2025; and

  b. The Special and Regular Meeting minutes of September 23, 2025.

11
WARRANT  The City Council unanimously approved the Warrant Register for October
  28, 2025, by motion of Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council
  Member Hurtado.

  Cancellations: None

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.
